entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.

decisions.decision: Madame de La Fayette’s classical analytic prose is kept: long periodic sentences, abstract moral vocabulary and restraint, without modernised casual speech.
decisions.rationale: The book is its analysis of passion and duty.

decisions.decision: The translation covers the publisher’s preface and the four parts exactly as Gutenberg #18797 prints them.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Reverses who marries whom in the arrangement with the King of Scotland.
The connétable is the object of “éloigna”; the translation made the king the one sent away.
“Cette reine” is the Dauphine; the sense was reversed.
“La reine, sa femme” is the Dauphin’s wife, the Dauphine, not the queen.
Madame de Clèves speaks to the Dauphine; the speaker and address form were wrong.
“De l’avoir perdue” refers to Madame de Tournon, a woman; the translation read “nó” (it).
Reversed sense: she had found him pleasing at about the time he loved her, not the reverse.
“Vu” means read, not heard: the tales the Dauphine means are ones you have read.
Wrong location and referent: the Vidame goes to Nemours’s house and into Nemours’s bedroom.
“Cette princesse” is the queen, not a young princess.
“Soit vue” (be seen) was negated in the translation.
The speaker is Madame de Clèves addressing the Dauphine; the referent was wrong.
The subject of “enverrait quérir” is Madame de Clèves, not the dauphine.
The second “ce prince” refers to Nemours, not to a different man.
“Ce n’est pas de vous dont vous parlez”: Nemours is not speaking about himself; the translation made it about the friend.
“Ce prince tomba” is the King (Henri II), who has just been wounded; the translation made him a prince.
“Les cachets de ce prince” are the King’s seals; the translation gave them to the prince.
Referent error in the clause about the children not resembling their father.
“Il lui fut impossible de demeurer chez la reine” refers to the Dauphine, not the queen.
Reversed sense in Nemours’s soliloquy.
“Ne cherchent que l’honneur de vous séduire” means their only aim is the glory of seducing you; the idiom was misread.
The referent was flipped in the clause about being saved from extravagances.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.source_term: Madame de Clèves / Monsieur de Nemours / Madame de Chartres
glossary.draft_rendering: bà de Clèves; ông de Nemours; bà de Chartres
glossary.rationale: Narration names fixed as in the glossary.

glossary.source_term: La vertu / la passion / le devoir / le repos
glossary.draft_rendering: đức hạnh; đam mê; bổn phận; sự yên ổn
glossary.rationale: One rendering of each abstract term.

glossary.rationale: Stable forms of address through the book.
Title as chosen for this edition.

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #18797, an electronic transcription of La Princesse de Clèves. The Gutenberg page does not name the exact printing and the text was not collated with the 1678 first edition.

title_review.rationale: The title follows the glossary and catalog choice, ‘Công nương xứ Clèves’ (The Princess of Clèves).

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The publisher’s preface, “LE LIBRAIRE AU LECTEUR.”, rendered “NGƯỜI XUẤT BẢN GỬI ĐỘC GIẢ.”
The last unit of the witness, the final unit of the Quatrième partie.
